title: Knowledge Check 1 - Lessons 1-5
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 1-5 - Permissions to Standard Objects, Custom Objects, and Fields. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: An architect needs to let a small group of support managers read every Account record, including records owned by other divisions, without granting them system administration. Which approach best fits?
options: Give each manager a profile with Read on Account
Create a permission set granting View All on Account and assign it to the managers
Set the Account org-wide default to Public Read Only
Give the managers Modify All on Account
questions.explanation: View All on Account bypasses sharing so they can read all records without any admin/system permission. Changing the OWD affects everyone, and Modify All also grants Edit, exceeding the need.

questions.question: Which statement about profiles versus permission sets is TRUE?
options: Permission sets can remove object permissions granted by the profile
A user must be assigned at least one permission set
Permission sets add permissions on top of the profile and never take them away
Profiles can be assigned multiple per user
questions.explanation: Permission sets are purely additive; the profile is the single baseline and permission sets extend it. A user can have zero permission sets and exactly one profile.

questions.question: Why is a permission set group preferable to assigning several individual permission sets to a large cohort of users?
options: It bundles multiple permission sets so users receive the combined permissions with one assignment, and it supports dynamic assignment
It can remove a permission that the profile grants to all users
It changes the users' profile automatically
It grants record access without any object permissions
questions.explanation: A permission set group packages several permission sets for a single assignment and supports dynamic assignment rules, reducing admin overhead for large cohorts. It cannot remove profile permissions, change profiles, or grant record access by itself.

questions.question: An admin must grant 400 sales users Edit access to a custom object, but only a handful of execs should see it at all. What is the cleanest approach?
options: Add Edit to the sales profile for everyone
Create a permission set granting Edit, put it in a group, and dynamically assign the group to sales users
Create a separate profile for each exec
Make the custom object's OWD Public Read/Write
questions.explanation: A permission set + group + dynamic assignment scales to 400 users without bloating the profile or changing sharing. Editing the shared profile grants it to non-sales users too, and OWD changes affect everyone.

questions.question: A permission set exists to grant access to a paid managed-package object, but assigning it to a user produces a license error. What is the most likely cause?
options: The user's profile has the object on page layout
The permission set is qualified for a license the user does not have
The object is standard
The profile already grants View All
questions.explanation: Managed-package object permissions are license-gated; if the permission set is tied to a license the user lacks, assignment fails. The other choices do not cause a license error.

questions.question: Which is the recommended pattern for scaling a permission grant to a large, frequently-changing user population?
options: Edit the standard profile each time a new hire starts
Create a permission set group and use dynamic assignment rules on user attributes
Manually assign individual permission sets to each user
Set the object OWD to Public Read Only
questions.explanation: Dynamic assignment on a permission set group automatically covers joiners/leavers by filter criteria, the most scalable and least manual pattern.

questions.question: A Sales user should see the Opportunity Amount but never the Discount custom field. What field permission change is required?
options: Set Discount to Read-Only
Set Discount to Hidden
Remove Discount from the page layout only
Set Amount to Hidden
questions.explanation: Hidden is the only FLS state that removes the field from view for that user. Read-Only still displays it, layout removal alone leaves it exposed via search/reports, and hiding Amount is the opposite of the need.

questions.question: Which statement about field-level security is TRUE?
options: A user who can read an object always sees every field
Hidden fields are still returned by user-mode Apex SOQL unless enforced
Read-only fields are invisible to the user
FLS only applies to custom fields
questions.explanation: User-mode Apex returns hidden fields unless the code applies Security Enforced or StripInaccessible; FLS is not automatic in all code paths. Reading an object does not grant field visibility, and FLS applies to standard fields too.

questions.question: Why is removing a field from a page layout alone insufficient to secure a sensitive standard field?
options: Layout changes apply to all users
The field can still appear in search, list views, and reports where FLS is not honored
Standard fields cannot be secured
Layouts do not control standard objects
questions.explanation: Page layouts only affect record pages; search, list views, and reports surface fields by FLS, so a field visible in FLS but absent from a layout is still exposed in those surfaces.

questions.question: Management wants the Phone field read-only for support users but fully editable for sales. Which change applies the cleanest?
options: Set Phone to Read-Only in the support profile (or a support permission set) and leave it editable in the sales profile
Hide Phone for the whole org
Create two record types for the object
Change the Phone field to a formula
questions.explanation: FLS is per-profile/permission-set, so read-only for support and editable for sales is exactly the profile-level difference FLS provides. Hiding removes it for everyone, and record types do not control field editing.

questions.question: Which scenario is best solved with record types rather than field-level security?
options: Hiding a custom SSN field from all reps
Giving different sales processes different picklist values and page layouts by deal type
Preventing a user from editing the Owner field
Hiding a field from reports
questions.explanation: Record types tailor layouts, business processes, and picklist values by profile. FLS alone cannot present different picklist sets or layouts per process; it only controls field visibility/editing.

questions.question: A user can edit the Account Rating field on the record page even though the field was removed from their page layout. What is the most likely reason?
options: Record types are disabled
FLS still grants edit permission for Rating
The field is standard
The user is the owner
questions.explanation: Page layout absence does not revoke the FLS edit permission; the user can still edit via other surfaces or the field being FLS-editable. The fix is to set the field read-only in FLS, not just remove it from a layout.

questions.question: A company hides the Compensation custom field from the sales profile's page layout, but a report still shows the value. Why?
options: Record types are misconfigured
UI hiding does not secure the field from reports; FLS must hide it
The report runs in system mode
Compensation is a standard field
questions.explanation: Page layout hiding only affects record pages; reports, list views, and search honor FLS. The durable fix is setting the field to Hidden in field-level security, not just removing it from the layout.

questions.question: Which mechanism best tailors record-page fields and picklist values to different business processes for the same object?
options: Compact layouts
Record types plus page layouts
Sharing rules
Field-level security alone
questions.explanation: Record types + page layouts vary the record page and picklist values by process. Compact layouts only affect the highlight panel, and FLS/Sharing do not define processes.

questions.question: A field visible in field-level security but removed from a page layout can still leak data. Which surface is the primary leak?
options: Reports
The org-wide default
Apex trigger debug logs
The record owner field
questions.explanation: Reports (and list views and search) read from field-level security, so a field visible in FLS but absent from a layout still appears in reports. OWD, debug logs, and the owner field do not surface hidden-by-layout fields in this way.
